rules.text: Do not introduce repeated or unbounded memory leaks to obtain a static lifetime when the data should be owned, borrowed or shared for a bounded operation. An intentional bounded process-lifetime allocation during initialization is allowed.

question.instructions: Does added code create a 'static reference by abandoning ownership of a heap allocation on a path that runs for each request or item?

criteria.true: A per-request, per-item or otherwise unbounded path leaks an owned allocation to produce a 'static reference, with no reclamation contract. Repeated calls retain additional allocations. Box::leak in a request handler is an example, not the only mechanism.
criteria.false: No such allocation-to-static-reference path is added; the retained allocation occurs only once during process initialization; or ownership is transferred to a component that later frees it. Static types and unsafe code alone do not qualify.

rules.text: Avoid deep cloning or allocating an owned copy solely to inspect unchanged data when an ordinary borrow is sufficient. Owned results are appropriate when independence, mutation, storage or a snapshot is part of the actual contract.

question.instructions: Does new code unnecessarily copy an unchanged value just to read it? Classify by whether a borrow satisfies the actual consumer contract.

criteria.true: For example: records.clone().len(); buffer.to_vec().iter().any(predicate); cloning a configuration only to inspect a field. The owned value has the same representation and a borrow would satisfy both the API and lifetime.
criteria.false: For example: encode text into a byte representation required by a protocol; construct a validated value; clone a result that must outlive its owner; transfer owned data to a worker. These uses require transformation or ownership. No such unnecessary copy is also false.
